main_body: A steampunk lamp-post: a domed grey metal cap at the top (rows 1-9), a glowing orange lantern box (rows 11-16), a thin pole with a collar, and a domed grey metal base (rows 36-44).
top_band: Lighter grey domed cap at rows ~2-6, with a gold highlight; the dome is rounded and reads as a surface seen from above, though it is a dome rather than a flat ellipse. The pedestal at rows ~37-40 also has a lighter grey top.
evidence: Reading a column through the middle: the top cap shows a lighter grey dome (about 5 rows) with a gold highlight, then a darker slate underside (rows 7-9) that acts as an eave shadow over the lantern. The base has a lighter domed top (rows 37-40) above a darker front face (rows 41-44). The main body, a thin pole of 2-3 px width, is a narrow shaft. The caps read as rounded surfaces seen from above, similar to the ellipse-cap column in the guide. No distinct front-edge line is drawn, but the tone steps are clear, and the lantern windows are inset with dark frames. The thin pole is a minor part of the design. I judge it three_quarter, though marginally so.

style.evidence: The metal ramps carry about 4 grey steps (highlight, light, mid, dark, slate), plus the orange glow with 3 tones. The outline is a dark near-black with a bluish lean, only partly material-toned, and is clearly used on the cap and base edges. The pole is a flat 2-3 px wide fill, and the cap and base have only sparse texture, with no rivets or grain. The tiles carry fewer colours than the reference stall and well, which have per-tile highlights and grain. It reads as a little thinner and more sticker-like than the Beodeul references.
